title: S 84 (124th General Assembly): Voter ID
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id) not stated.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) Sec. 1 (7-13-710(D)(1)(a))
(quote) If an elector does not produce a valid and current photograph identification due to a religious objection to being photographed, he may complete a written statement under penalty of perjury at the polling place and affirm that the elector: (i) is the same individual who personally appeared at the polling place; (ii) cast the provisional ballot on election day; and (iii) has a religious objection to being photographed.
(section) Sec. 1 (7-13-710(D)(1)(b))
(quote) If an elector does not produce a valid and current photograph identification because the elector suffers from a reasonable impediment that prevents the elector from obtaining photograph identification, he may complete a written statement under the penalty of perjury at the polling place
(section) Sec. 1 (7-13-710(D)(2))
(quote) If the county board of registration and elections determines that the voter was challenged only for the inability to provide proof of identification and the required written statement is submitted, the county board of registration and elections shall find that the provisional ballot is valid unless the board has grounds to believe the written statement is false.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule) not stated.
(other) Sec. 2: effective on approval by the Governor.
(other) version: Only one version (Introduced, 2020-12-09). Slot b only: replaces the word 'affidavit' with 'written statement' throughout 7-13-710(D)(1)-(2); the religious-objection and reasonable-impediment remedies and the provisional ballot are otherwise reprinted unchanged.
(other) note: Only the introduced text is saved. Wording change only: 'an affidavit' becomes 'a written statement'; the struck word is 'affidavit'.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
